county_relationship.note: Counties derived from the county on each facility's source record. A ZIP can span several counties; HUD USPS crosswalk not yet configured.

top_violation_types.title: Employee record: Signed and Dated Statement for Orientation/Pre-Service training  by trainer and employee (26 TAC §746.1329(d))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: One caregiver who the director stated received orientation during hire did not have documentation of the verified orientation.    This was corrected during inspection with the director and caregiver signing completion of orientation.

top_violation_types.title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Use Praise and Encouragement (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(A))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: A caregiver was observed on video grabbing several children by one arm and forcibly moving them from one place to the other in the classroom.

top_violation_types.title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The ground is splitting open and causing a tripping hazard at the entrance to the playground.       Photos taken

top_violation_types.title: Maximum Height - Under Age 2 (26 TAC §746.4607(b)(1))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: During the investigation, it was stated the victim was seen playing on play structure over 32 inches.

top_violation_types.title: Employee Handwashing After Diapering a Child (26 TAC §746.3415(4))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: A caregiver did not wash their hands after changing a child's diaper.

top_violation_types.title: Activities for Infants - Not in Restrictive Device for more than 15 Minutes (26 TAC §746.2417(2)(B))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Children are left in buggies longer than fiftteen minutes which is the maximum time frame a child may be in a restrictive device.

top_violation_types.title: HRC42.052(c) - AP Illegal Operation - Not Listed (26 TAC §HRC42.052(c) - AP Illegal Operation - No)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Regular care is being provided to 2 unrelated children.

top_violation_types.title: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - installed and maintained according to manufacturer's instructions (26 TAC §746.5625(b))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The electronic child safety alarm was observed not functioning in one of the operation's vans used to transport the children in care.
